title: Sedro-Woolley to turn back on its Flock cameras
byline: VINCE RICHARDSON, Skagit Valley Herald, Mount Vernon, Wash.
summary: The Sedro-Woolley City Council voted to reactivate its seven Flock ALPR cameras, which had been disabled in June 2025 after a public records request, following new Washington state legislation restricting access and use. Police Chief Dan McIlraith expects the cameras back online by June 1 and negotiated a prorated discount with Flock. The article also notes Stanwood reactivated its cameras in April and that both cities are appealing a Skagit County ruling that ALPR images are subject to the state Public Records Act.

key_quotes.quote: The Sedro-Woolley City Council voted Wednesday night to turn back on the city's Flock Safety Camera System.
Sedro-Woolley's seven Flock cameras went live in March 2025 and were disabled in June 2025 after a public records request was filed for images taken by the cameras.

A new state law limits images to authorized law enforcement personnel for valid law enforcement purposes. Federal agencies are prohibited from accessing Flock camera data, including for immigration enforcement.

The cities of Sedro-Woolley and Stanwood are asking a state appeals court to reverse a Skagit County Superior Court ruling that prior to the new law being signed images taken by the cameras were subject to the state Public Records act.
